# Diagnostics

<!-- Generated by `node docs/gen-diagnostics.ts` from compiler/diagnostics.ts, LANGUAGE.md and docs/guide.md. Do not edit: edit compiler/diagnostics.ts and run it again. `node docs/gen-diagnostics.ts --check` (in proof/all.ts) fails when this file is stale; test/diagnostics.ts fails when a code the compiler gives has no row, or no test that makes the compiler give it. -->

A code starts with the part of the compiler that gives it: L for the lexer (the characters of a file), P for the parser (its shape), C for the checker and the rules (what it means). A refusal is a code, a file and line, what is wrong there, and what to write instead; the line and the fix name what the program wrote. This page says what each code refuses whatever the program, and where [LANGUAGE.md](../LANGUAGE.md) or [the guide](guide.md) explains it.

109 codes.

| Code | Refuses | Explained in |
|---|---|---|
| L01 | A character Tape does not have outside a text literal or a comment. A `!`, a `;`, a `?`, a backtick, and the doubled & and \| of other languages are each named, with what Tape writes instead. |  |
| L02 | A text literal not closed on its line. Text is on one line; a backslash at the end of a line carries it on. |  |
| L03 | An escape a text literal does not have. Text allows `\" \\ \/ \n \r \t \b \f`, and a hole for a value. |  |
| L04 | A migration's SQL with no closing `}`, so the rest of the file would be read as SQL. |  |
| L05 | A hole in a text literal that is not closed, or that holds a text literal: a hole holds one expression with no text in it. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text) |
| L06 | A number Tape does not have: an exponent without the `f` of a Float, a Dec with more than 18 digits after the point, or a Float with more than 20 significant digits or past the largest Float. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text) |
| L07 | A byte literal that is not one byte: empty, two characters, a character past ASCII, a raw control character, an unknown escape, or not closed. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text); [the guide: Patterns](guide.md#patterns) |
| P01 | The parser expected one token and found another: most often a reserved word where a name goes, a `let` with a type, or a pattern that is an expression to compute. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text); [the guide: Patterns](guide.md#patterns) |
| P02 | Where an expression goes, something that is not one. It names the forms Tape does not have (`if`, `return`, tuples) and a line that starts with `-`, which starts a new value. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text) |
| P03 | Comparisons chained, `a < b < c`. A comparison is a Bool, and two are joined with `and`. |  |
| P04 | Where a pattern goes, something that is not one: a reserved word, `else` in a match on a value (its fallback is `_`), or `pattern ++` with no text literal after it. |  |
| P05 | At the top of a file, something that is not a declaration. A file is `fn`, `type`, `interface`, `migration`, `schema`, `flag`, `machine` and `invariant`; a statement goes inside a function. |  |
| P06 | An interface method that does not say `read` or `write`. It says whether a call may be repeated as it is or carries a key. |  |
| P07 | The right side of a pipe is not a function call, so there is nothing to pass the value to. | [the guide: Pipes and ++](guide.md#pipes-and-) |
| P08 | A literal outside its type: an Int past 64 bits, or a Dec past the 64-bit count of its scale. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text); [the guide: Numbers: exact, or a trap](guide.md#numbers-exact-or-a-trap) |
| P09 | An expression nested more than 500 deep (a match or a lambda counts four). The parser stops there rather than run out of stack; name a part with `let`. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text) |
| C01 | A type or interface declared twice, or with the name of a built-in type. A name means one type. | [the guide: Names: a program's own wins over std's](guide.md#names-a-programs-own-wins-over-stds) |
| C02 | A type with no constructors. It would have no values, so nothing could be made or matched. |  |
| C03 | A constructor declared twice. A constructor belongs to one type, so a pattern or a call of it means one thing. | [the guide: Names: a program's own wins over std's](guide.md#names-a-programs-own-wins-over-stds) |
| C04 | A function defined twice in one file, or a method listed twice in one interface. | [LANGUAGE.md: 4. Functions](../LANGUAGE.md#4-functions); [the guide: Names: a program's own wins over std's](guide.md#names-a-programs-own-wins-over-stds) |
| C05 | A type given the wrong number of type arguments: `Dec` without its scale, `Rows` without one row type, a declared type with more or fewer than it takes. |  |
| C06 | A type name that nothing declares. |  |
| C07 | A type laid out inside itself, which would have no end. A type that holds itself through a field is boxed; today only a type parameter with the name of its own type reaches this. |  |
| C08 | A capability bound with `let`, or a Buf or a capability as a field. A Buf has one owner at a time and a capability is passed by name, so neither is stored. | [LANGUAGE.md: 9. One way to do each job](../LANGUAGE.md#9-one-way-to-do-each-job) |
| C09 | A type that cannot be a row type, decoded from JSON or written as JSON, for a field neither holds; or a function value whose parameter takes a name already in use. | [LANGUAGE.md: 9. One way to do each job](../LANGUAGE.md#9-one-way-to-do-each-job) |
| C10 | An argument after the first with no name, or a pattern for a field that does not name it. A call and a pattern say which value is which. | [LANGUAGE.md: 4. Functions](../LANGUAGE.md#4-functions); [the guide: Numbers: exact, or a trap](guide.md#numbers-exact-or-a-trap) |
| C11 | An argument the function, constructor, method or built-in does not take. | [LANGUAGE.md: 4. Functions](../LANGUAGE.md#4-functions) |
| C12 | One argument given twice (by name after a pipe already gave the first parameter, too), or a function value called with other than its arguments, in order and unnamed. | [the guide: Pipes and ++](guide.md#pipes-and-) |

| C14 | A value of one type where another is expected. | C15 | A name bound again in one function. Names are never reused, so each means one value. |  |
| C16 | A name that is not a parameter, a `let` or a pattern binding in scope. | [LANGUAGE.md: 5. Patterns](../LANGUAGE.md#5-patterns) |
| C17 | A dot on a value of a type with several constructors. Only a one-constructor type has fields. |  |
| C18 | A field the value's type does not have, read with a dot or named in a pattern; or a function pattern given more than one pattern. |  |
| C19 | An operator its operands do not have: `++` on what is not text, `/` and `%` on a Dec, `%` on a Float, a comparison of Options, a value in a text hole that is not text or a number, a literal pattern for a Dec or a Float. | [LANGUAGE.md: 2. Text](../LANGUAGE.md#2-text) |
| C20 | A constructor that nothing declares. | [LANGUAGE.md: 3. Types](../LANGUAGE.md#3-types); [the guide: A machine's states in a match](guide.md#a-machines-states-in-a-match) |
| C21 | A constructor of a generic type, such as `None`, used where nothing says which type it is (`Option[Int]` or `Option[View]`). | [LANGUAGE.md: 4. Functions](../LANGUAGE.md#4-functions) |
| C22 | A function that nothing defines, called or used as a pattern. |  |
| C23 | A match the value cannot have: a constructor of another type, a constructor pattern on a type with none, or a match on a Buf or a capability. |  |
| C24 | A match that does not cover every value of its subject, or a condition match without its last `else`. A match always says what it is. | [LANGUAGE.md: 4. Functions](../LANGUAGE.md#4-functions); [the guide: Patterns](guide.md#patterns) |
| C25 | A Buf used after it was handed over. A Buf has one owner at a time. | [LANGUAGE.md: 3. Types](../LANGUAGE.md#3-types) |
| C26 | A Buf handed over inside a guard, a condition, a pattern, a destructuring `let` or the right side of `and`/`or`, which may not run. |  |
| C27 | A Buf that is never used: its bytes would be lost. Return it, pass it on, or freeze it. |  |
| C28 | Match arms that hand over different Bufs. Each arm uses the same ones, so each Buf has one owner after the match. |  |

| C96 | A status written as a literal that the host refuses: outside 200 to 599, or a 204, 205 or 304 given a body (`empty(status: 204)` has none); or a `problem` whose status is not an error (200 to 399). A status that is a value is checked when the host answers, which says why in a 500. | [LANGUAGE.md: 6. Effects](../LANGUAGE.md#6-effects) |
| C97 | A match on a machine's states with an arm that takes the states the arms beside it do not name (`_`, a name, a row pattern that leaves the state out). A state added to the machine would be taken there without a word; each state gets an arm of its own. | [LANGUAGE.md: 5. Patterns](../LANGUAGE.md#5-patterns); [the guide: Rules: writes that survive a retry, migrations that only add](guide.md#rules-writes-that-survive-a-retry-migrations-that-only-add) |
| C98 | The error of an exported method, or the `error:` a `call` or an `ask` names, that is not a type of the program's own with constructors (a View, an Int, a std type): the callee's refusals are the constructors a caller matches `Rejected(reason: …)` on, each of them, and text gives a match nothing to hold to. `woken`'s error may be text, as the host only logs it; a capability's (an `interface`) is text. | [LANGUAGE.md: 6. Effects](../LANGUAGE.md#6-effects) |
| C99 | A compiler bug, not a mistake in the program: a type not known where it must be, a function value of no function, a match with no arms, a std type not as the compiler expects. Report it with the program. |  |
| C100 | A fetch whose method is not written `Get` or `Head` without `key: Some(…)`. A request that timed out may have been received, so it is sent again, which is safe only when the other side can tell it for a repeat: std/http.tape's fetch sends the key as Idempotency-Key. | [LANGUAGE.md: 6. Effects](../LANGUAGE.md#6-effects) |
| C101 | A signature that does not say which capabilities its function reaches: a function that uses one by name, itself or through what it calls, without `uses` and those names in alphabetical order after its result type (`uses clock, db`), a clause that names one it does not reach, or a clause on an entry point, which declares each capability as a parameter. `tape fmt` writes the clause. | [LANGUAGE.md: 1. What a program is](../LANGUAGE.md#1-what-a-program-is); [the guide: Capabilities by name](guide.md#capabilities-by-name) |

## Reserved

These codes are kept for rules that are written down and not shipped. The compiler gives none of them.

| Code | For |
|---|---|
| C89 | a Float as a SQL parameter; reserved by docs/numbers-language-draft.md (spec Q12), not shipped |
| C90 | a Float in a call's key; reserved by docs/numbers-language-draft.md (spec Q12), not shipped |
| C91 | a take-from-quantity or compare-and-set on a REAL column; reserved by docs/numbers-language-draft.md (spec Q12), not shipped |
| C92 | a Dec meeting a column that does not hold it; reserved by docs/numbers-language-draft.md (spec Q12), not shipped |
